## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization of the per-particle update loop can approach the streaming ceiling on low-churn workloads.

## Cache saturation
All tested N values (10000–10000000) exceed the L2 spill at N≈7710; N=1000000 and N=10000000 also exceed the L3 spill at N≈246723. At q=0.01, ns/p rises modestly from 24.498 (N=10000) to 26.52 (N=1000000), then holds at 26.204 (N=10000000) — a ~7% drift across the L2→DRAM transition with no sharp knee. Death rate raises the floor without reshaping the curve: q=0.5 sits at ~33.5 ns/p across all N versus ~25 ns/p at q=0.01. The N-shape is essentially flat within every death-rate band, indicating cost is dominated by per-particle work rather than cache capacity.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved is 2.78 GB/s at N=10000, q=0.01 — 22% of the 12.69 GB/s streaming ceiling. Bandwidth stays nearly constant across N (2.56–2.78 GB/s at q=0.01) and declines with death rate, falling to 2.01 GB/s at q=0.5. The algo is neither bandwidth-bound nor compute-bound: frontend_stall dominates at 63–70% across all profiles, backend_stall is 0%, and compute sits at 30–37%. It is overhead-bound — specifically frontend-bound — with no transition point by N or death rate; the frontend bottleneck is present from the smallest N and persists uniformly.

## Assembly
The compiler vectorized across the components of a single particle, not across particles. `vmovups xmm0,[rbx]` loads 16 bytes of position, followed by `vmulps`/`vaddps` packed operations on those four floats, with `vshufps` and `vinsertps` for lane rearrangement. No gather instruction appears. The render pass performs byte-granular scatter stores: `mov BYTE PTR [r13+r14*1+0x0],dl` with `cmovae` saturation to 0xff, repeated per RGBA channel. The 345-instruction function carries 27 `cmp`, 11 `jae`, and 7 `jmp`, reflecting heavy branching from respawn logic and bounds-checked scatter — this explains the 63–70% frontend stall. Component-wise packed math on four floats per particle cannot compensate for the scalar byte-scatter and branchy control flow.

## Verdict
Refuted — achieved bandwidth never exceeds 2.78 GB/s (22% of the 12.69 GB/s ceiling) at any N or death rate. The compiler produced component-wise packed math (`vmulps`/`vaddps`) but the 345-instruction branchy step function with byte-granular scatter stores drives frontend_stall to 63–70%, making the algo overhead-bound rather than bandwidth-bound. Auto-vectorization over per-particle components cannot approach the streaming ceiling.
